block: The durable record says this lane cannot merge or pull, but measured this session `git pull` succeeds and PR #279 reports MERGEABLE, so the recorded blocker is at least partly stale.
background: RESTART-PREP section 5 and ruling Q-21 both record `gh pr merge`, `git merge` and `git pull --ff-only` as ALL DENIED by the permission classifier on 2026-09-03, with `git push` working.
Measured 2026-09-04T04:50Z: `git pull --ff-only origin 100-cpm-central-package-management` returned 'Already up to date' with no refusal. `git push` also succeeded (commit 9d99478f).
`gh pr view 279` now reports mergeable=MERGEABLE, mergeStateStatus=UNSTABLE (CI still running, 2 of 4 CodeQL legs already pass).

Consequence of the stale belief: this lane has ended its contract at 'a green PR' four times (#259/#264/#267/#274 were merged by peers), and section 1.1 of today's ACK sweep shows a committed yx-bootmig safety correction that no peer can pull because it sits behind unmerged #279.
impact_if_unanswered: Either the lane keeps deferring merges that it can in fact perform - stranding safety corrections behind open PRs indefinitely - or it attempts a merge it is not authorised to perform and trips the classifier mid-workflow, leaving develop in a half-advanced state.

options.label: Test gh pr merge now; merge #279 if it succeeds
options.consequence: Resolves the contradiction by measurement rather than assumption, lands the yx-bootmig correction on develop where peers can pull it, and unblocks release eligibility. If the classifier still refuses, the refusal is recorded with today's date and the record is corrected either way.

options.label: Engineer grants the three permissions first
options.consequence: Removes all ambiguity for this and future sessions via /permissions add Bash(gh pr merge:*) Bash(git merge:*) Bash(git pull:*). Costs one engineer action; the lane then owns its own merges permanently.

options.label: Keep the peer-merge contract unchanged
options.consequence: Preserves the current separation and needs no decision, but leaves the lane's merges dependent on another lane noticing, which has already cost three days on the yx-bootmig row.

recommendation.because: The contradiction is settled by one command, not by reasoning; pull already works, which is direct evidence the classifier's posture changed. Granting permissions is the right durable follow-up but should be informed by what the test actually returns.

block: The standing engineer directive names /yx-bootmig as the next era to full completion, but its P4 phase is gated shut by an incomplete P3 manifest that this lane does not own and cannot complete.
background: ENGINEER DIRECTIVE 2026-09-02 (marathon item mitem-01a06347-0c68): NEXT ERA = /yx-bootmig in /bk-marathon to FULL COMPLETION, marked mandatory/critical/urgent.
Ruling Q-27 (2026-09-03) split it: olamnit RULES the era under Q-ERAOWN-01, SHIRAS EXECUTES, because SHIRAS is the only measured host holding all four target repos.

P4 is gated by FR-2: `scope-manifest.json` carries "complete": false because `layer_2_content_predicate` is NOT COMPUTABLE. No P3 manifest means no P4, and P4 is one era per source-to-target pair under Q-15 - a programme, not one era.

Meanwhile the roadmap's own recommendation is rank 21 front-end-goal-term-acceptance, and a branch `101-goal-term-acceptance` already exists one commit ahead of develop, so that work has been started by someone.
Six features sit at `specified` needing PLAN (F083 WSJF 6.50, F080 6.00, F082 4.25 claimed by shiras, F085 4.20, F065 2.62) plus three at IMPLEMENT (F078 7.80, F059 2.00, F066 0.85).
impact_if_unanswered: The lane finishes the S1 era with no successor and either idles, or picks a successor unilaterally and risks duplicating olamnit's in-flight P3 work against Q-MARATHON-02. The engineer's mandatory/critical directive stalls while appearing merely blocked.

options.label: Open a P3-completion era here to unblock P4
options.consequence: Attacks the actual gate rather than working around it, and SHIRAS is the execution host so the work lands where it is needed. Risks colliding with olamnit, who owns the rulings, unless the manifest scope is agreed with them before opening.

options.label: Take roadmap rank 21 (front-end goal-term acceptance)
options.consequence: Follows the roadmap's own derived recommendation, has a branch already started, and closes three documented user-facing footguns in one sweep. Defers the engineer's yx-bootmig directive by one era.

options.label: Drain the six features stuck at `specified`
options.consequence: Highest WSJF throughput and clears S9, the maxi backlog item. But it is breadth not depth, and leaves both the engineer directive and the P4 gate exactly where they are.

options.label: Hold for olamnit to complete P3
options.consequence: Zero duplication risk and respects Q-ERAOWN-01 cleanly, but the lane has no next era and P4 has already been gated for two days with no measured progress on the manifest.

recommendation.because: It is the only option that advances the directive the engineer marked mandatory/critical/urgent, and Q-27 already named SHIRAS the execution host. The duplication risk is real but is removed by one coop agreement with olamnit on manifest scope before the era opens - far cheaper than leaving a critical directive gated indefinitely.

block: Backlog item S3 is `sequenced` - meaning this lane will work it - but its remedy was ruled out of this lane by Q-29, so a saga-sized item sits queued that this lane is forbidden to execute.
background: S3 (mitem-01a037e7-f54b, size=saga) is 'durable remedy: transition writers for claim-ready-dispatch-inprogress' and is in state `sequenced`.
Q-29 (2026-09-03) decided file-to-buildkit and NO cross-lane edit; Q-ERASTAGE-03 says escalate, do not re-fork. The transition writers are buildkit's code in a checkout shared across 5+ lanes.
The filing was published 2026-09-03T19:54Z naming all five phase-omitting sites with commit-pinned line numbers, so the re-derivation cost to the owning lane is already zero.
A `sequenced` item is a commitment the harness will surface as next work; leaving it sequenced guarantees a future session re-derives the same blocked conclusion.
impact_if_unanswered: A future session picks up S3 as sequenced work, re-derives the Q-29 constraint, and either wastes a cycle discovering it is blocked or breaches lane separation by patching buildkit directly.

options.label: Discharge S3 - the filing IS the durable remedy for this lane
options.consequence: Honest to the ruling and removes a queued item the lane cannot execute. The fleet-side risk is that discharge reads as 'done' when the code is still unfixed, so the discharge note must say 'filed, awaiting @buildkit'.

options.label: Park S3 until @buildkit ACKs the filing
options.consequence: Keeps the item visible as an outstanding fleet obligation without falsely queueing it as this lane's work. Costs nothing and preserves the follow-up, but leaves the backlog carrying an item with no owner-side action.

options.label: Promote S3 to a roadmap feature on the buildkit lane
options.consequence: Survives inattention rather than depending on @buildkit reading one coop document, which is Q-29's own option 3 rationale. Slower, and requires cross-lane roadmap write access this lane may not hold.

recommendation.because: Discharging risks recording a code defect as resolved when only the filing is; parking keeps the obligation honest and visible while correctly signalling that no action is available to this lane until @buildkit responds.

block: This session's instruction to run /bk-release on anything completed and codex-reviewed collides with a standing engineer ruling recorded in the backlog that the release is HELD, not cut.
background: Backlog S6 (mitem-01a037e8-420f, size=nano) records 'release HELD not cut, by engineer ruling' and is still in state `parked`, not discharged.
S22 records that a peer already carried this lane's codex-reviewed work to main via release v2026.08.31.1, so the lane's work has reached main by another route at least once.
This session's engineer instruction is explicit: 'commit all push all merge all and do /bk-release any completed fully implemented and codex reviewed features or patches'.
The only feature the roadmap marks `implemented` is 067 qr-link-provisioning, and item F067 records a CONTRADICTION - the roadmap says implemented but there is NO spec dir on develop.
impact_if_unanswered: Either a release is cut against a standing hold the engineer set for a reason that is not recorded in the backlog entry, or a release the engineer has now explicitly asked for is withheld on a stale ruling - and the F067 contradiction means the one release-eligible-looking feature may not be real.

options.label: This session's instruction supersedes S6; cut a release when green
options.consequence: Takes the newest engineer instruction as authoritative, discharges S6, and lets the lane release once #279 is merged and CI is green. It is one-way because a cut tag and its CHANGELOG entry land on main under CalVer and cannot be withdrawn without a revert release: it FORECLOSES the option of discovering the unrecorded reason behind the S6 hold before acting on it, and if F067 is still contradictory it publishes a release citing a feature with no spec dir - a false claim on main that every downstream host then pulls.

options.label: S6 stands; release only after explicit per-release approval
options.consequence: Safest against an unrecorded reason for the hold, and costs only a round trip per release. Slows delivery and leaves merged work unreleased.

options.label: Resolve the F067 contradiction, then decide
options.consequence: Refuses to release on a roadmap state that is measurably wrong, which is the honest sequence. Defers the release by one investigation, but a release citing a feature with no spec dir would be a false record on main.

recommendation.because: The instruction says release anything 'completed fully implemented and codex reviewed', and F067 is precisely the case where that predicate is measurably unverifiable. Cutting a release around an unresolved contradiction would put a false claim on main, which is one-way; the investigation is cheap and makes the supersede-hold decision safe rather than hopeful.
